title: Start a desk pendulum from its start mark, holding its stand still, and press STOP on its third swing
instruction: Start the desk pendulum and stop it on its third swing. Hold the stand still by the brass knob on its left end the whole time, so it does not slide on the smooth worktop. With the other hand push the bob by its peg out to the red start mark on the scale, 20 degrees to the right, and let it go. Then count the swings: when the bob comes back to the right for the third time, press the red STOP button once, and its brake stops the pendulum hanging straight down. Don't touch the bob while it swings. Then let go and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Counting a repeating event that looks the same every time, and acting on the right repetition, needs memory: nothing in view records how many swings have gone by. People do this when timing oscillations in a lab, counting strokes or turns, or waiting out a number of cycles before stopping a machine.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. A desk pendulum, loose on the smooth table: its stand (0.30 kg) is a walnut base 22.5 cm deep, 44 cm wide and 2.2 cm thick, its front edge 18.5 cm forward, centred on the centre line, with a 2.8 cm square walnut post at the back, 39.5 cm tall, and a walnut arm reaching forward from its top to a brass pivot 30 cm forward on the centre line, 36 cm above the table. A brass knob (2 cm across, 2.5 cm tall) stands on each end of the base, 30 cm forward and 20 cm left and right of the centre line. The pendulum (0.18 kg) swings left and right from the pivot: a steel rod and a brass cylinder bob 4 cm across and 3.5 cm tall, its centre 30 cm below the pivot (6 cm above the table), with a knurled brass peg 1.2 cm thick sticking 7.5 cm out of its front toward the arms. Under the peg a brass scale on the base is marked every 5 degrees from 30 degrees left to 30 degrees right, with a red start mark at 20 degrees right. On the base's front-right corner, 22 cm forward and 17 cm right of the centre line, is the STOP button: a yellow box 4 cm square and 2.2 cm tall with a red mushroom cap 2.6 cm across, and a small brake lamp beside it (dark until braked). The pendulum starts hanging still, straight down. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The pendulum's angle is measured against the stand, positive to the left. The bob is let go from the start mark if a hand pushed it out to between 15 and 35 degrees to the right and both hands then leave it (every fingertip centre more than 2.8 cm from the peg's axis and 4.5 cm from the bob's centre). From then on, each time the swinging bob turns back at its far end on the left (more than 5 degrees out), one swing has gone by; the third swing ends as the bob comes back to the right, so STOP is on time if it is first pressed after the bob's third turn on the left and before its fourth. STOP is pressed when a fingertip centre is within 2 cm of the cap's axis and within 2 cm above its top for two control steps; the first press puts the brake on for good. 0.0 if at any time the stand moves more than 2.5 cm or tilts more than 8 degrees, or a hand comes to the bob (as above) after it was let go and before STOP. Otherwise, at the end: 1.0 with the bob let go from the start mark, STOP first pressed on time, the pendulum hanging within 3 degrees of straight down and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.75 with STOP first pressed on time but the pendulum not yet hanging still or the arms not home; 0.5 with the bob let go from the start mark and STOP pressed, but not on time; 0.25 with the bob let go from the start mark; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the stand and the pendulum still.
reset_notes: Let the pendulum hang still, straight down; put the stand back on its spot.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the pendulum turns on a nearly frictionless hinge, so its swing hardly dies away; the brake is the hinge's damping, switched up when STOP is pressed; the button is a fingertip near its cap, not a moving switch. The stand is lighter than a real one (0.30 kg) and slides easily on the smooth table. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
